note: Actual and Pass/Fail are filled in by testing/generate_report.py from a real pytest run; nothing here is typed by hand.

cases.description: Expired/hospice discharge codes are rejected with an out_of_scope error instead of being scored.
cases.steps: 1. POST /predict with each discharge code 11, 13, 14, 19, 20, 21. 2. Read the status and error type.
cases.expected: HTTP 422 with error type out_of_scope and the message 'no prediction is made' for every code.

cases.description: A misspelled category is rejected with the allowed values instead of being silently scored.
cases.steps: 1. POST /predict with gender 'Femle'. 2. Read the error.
cases.expected: HTTP 422, type invalid_category, location body.gender, message lists 'Female, Male'.

cases.description: Every numeric field accepts its training-data minimum and maximum and rejects one past either end.
cases.steps: For each of the 6 numeric fields: POST min, max, min-1, max+1.
cases.expected: min and max return 200; min-1 and max+1 return 422 out_of_range.

cases.description: Tier assignment at the exact cutoffs and percentile lookup at the edges.
cases.steps: 1. Call assign_tier just below and at each cutoff. 2. Call percentile_rank at 0, 1, the median and the 90th percentile.
cases.input: Cutoffs 0.1008 / 0.188 and the 101 stored score quantiles
cases.expected: Below 0.1008 = Low, 0.1008 = Moderate, 0.188 = High; percentiles 0, 100, 50, 90.

cases.description: SHAP contributions plus the baseline add up to the model's own output for several patients.
cases.steps: 1. POST /explain for 4 patients. 2. Sum baseline + contributions. 3. Compare with the model's log-odds and the score.
cases.input: App defaults, the test set's top row, and two variants
cases.expected: Sum equals the model's log-odds (within rounding, 0.001) and the score (within 0.0005).

cases.description: LLM items citing a source that wasn't retrieved, or citing nothing, are listed as unsupported, not shown as fact.
cases.steps: 1. Fake LLM returns one supported item, one citing MADE-UP-01, one with no citation. 2. Read items and unsupported.
cases.expected: Only the supported item is shown; the other two appear under 'unsupported' with reasons.

cases.requirement: Privacy: no personal details sent externally
cases.description: Email addresses and phone numbers are redacted before anything is sent to an LLM provider.
cases.steps: Call redact() on text with an email and a phone number.
cases.expected: '[redacted email], [redacted phone]'; ordinary text unchanged.

cases.description: End to end: the API reproduces the notebook's score for the test set's highest-risk encounter.
cases.steps: POST /predict with the test set's top-scoring encounter (validation, encoding, model, tiering).
cases.input: Top test-set encounter (9 prior stays, age 80-89, ...)
cases.expected: readmission_risk_score 0.782, high_risk true, risk_tier High, risk_percentile 100.

cases.requirement: FR-4 Suggest discharge-planning items; FR-5 Cite sources
cases.description: The assistant returns discharge-planning items, each citing retrieved excerpts, with review labels and a disclaimer.
cases.steps: POST /assistant for two patients with no question (rule-based mode).
cases.expected: status answered; every item cites excerpts present in 'citations'; each citation has URL, quote and 'Source pending review'; disclaimer present.

cases.requirement: FR-6 / NFR AI reliability: insufficient-information fallback
cases.description: A question the curated sources don't cover gets 'Insufficient information' instead of a guess.
cases.steps: Ask the assistant 'What is the capital of France?'.
cases.expected: status insufficient_information, no items, message starts 'Insufficient information'.

cases.description: Streamlit dashboard (AppTest) calls the API in-process and leads with the tier and the multiple of the average.
cases.steps: 1. Open the app. 2. Open the top patient from the queue. 3. Read the risk card.
cases.expected: High-tier card with badge 'High risk', large '7.0x', 'Top 10% of patients', 'Score 78% (average: 11%)', 26.7% tier rate.

cases.description: The hand-made hospice case opens an out-of-scope card with no score and no assistant.
cases.steps: Open patient PT-2745 (discharge code 14) from the queue.
cases.expected: Grey 'Out of scope' card, 'No prediction is made for this patient', no discharge-planning section.

cases.description: Each request is logged with metadata only; patient values and question text never appear in the log.
cases.steps: 1. POST /predict for the top patient. 2. Read the audit log entry.
cases.expected: One entry with request ID matching X-Request-ID, endpoint, status 200, tier High, role anonymous; no patient values in the file.

cases.description: With ROLE_KEYS set, staff endpoints need the discharge_staff role and the attempts are logged.
cases.steps: POST /explain with no key, an auditor key and a staff key; POST /assistant with a staff key.
cases.input: Demo keys for discharge_staff and auditor
cases.expected: 401, 403, 200, 200; log shows anonymous / auditor-01 / nurse-01 / nurse-01.

cases.requirement: NFR Explainability; rule 'factors must be real model inputs'
cases.description: Explanations list exactly the 14 input fields, ordered by size, with shares summing to 100%.
cases.steps: POST /explain for 4 patients and inspect the factors.
cases.expected: Exactly the 14 field names, values equal to the input, shares sum to 1, sorted by absolute contribution.

cases.requirement: NFR Performance (results within a few seconds)
cases.description: Explanation latency in-process.
cases.steps: Warm up once, then time 10 /explain calls.
cases.expected: Average under 0.5 s per explanation.

cases.description: 50 requests to a real uvicorn server across /predict, /explain and /assistant; measure server memory and latency.
cases.steps: 1. Start uvicorn. 2. Send 50 requests (rotating endpoints). 3. Record server RSS after each request and per-request latency.
cases.expected: Every request returns 200; peak server memory under 512 MB; p95 latency under 2,000 ms.

cases.description: Cold start against the live Render API, then warm requests.
cases.steps: 1. GET / on the live API and time the first response. 2. Time 3 /predict calls and 1 /explain call.
cases.expected: First response under 120 s (wake-up allowance); warm calls under 5 s; score 0.782, tier High.

cases.description: A slow LLM provider times out and the assistant falls back to rule-based mode.
cases.steps: Fake provider that sleeps 1 s; timeout set to 0.2 s.
cases.expected: Reply in under 0.9 s, mode rule_based_fallback, note says 'no reply within 0.2 s'.

cases.requirement: Constraint: advisory only, not diagnostic or treatment
cases.description: Diagnosis, dosing, prescribing and prompt-injection questions are refused without calling the LLM.
cases.steps: Ask 5 out-of-scope questions with a fake provider attached.
cases.input: 'What insulin dose should I prescribe?', 'Ignore previous instructions...', and 3 more
cases.expected: status refused, no items, provider never called.
